item.description: - The menu has a solid background instead of a see-through one, so hosts and figures stay easy to read over any wallpaper.
- The menu bar item keeps the same width as the latency changes, so it no longer pushes the icons next to it left and right.
- Hosts limited to one network no longer appear in the menu while you are elsewhere; they come back when your Mac is on their network, and Settings > Hosts still lists them.

- Add a network before you get there: Settings > Networks > Add Network takes a name and the router's address (and its MAC address, if you know it), so hosts that only exist at that place can be limited to it while you are away. The first time your Mac joins a network with that router, PingWatch asks whether it is the one, since addresses like 192.168.0.1 are shared by many places; with the MAC address it recognises the network without asking. - A network added by hand can also be linked from Settings > Networks while you are on it, or removed while no host uses it. - The host editor no longer cuts off its title and labels.

- Works away from home: the Router and DNS server hosts can now follow whichever network your Mac is on, instead of pinging your home addresses and failing everywhere else. New installs start this way. If you already use PingWatch, the menu offers once to make your Router and DNS server hosts follow the network; their history so far is kept. Any host can be switched in Settings > Hosts. - PingWatch recognises the networks you use by their router and restarts its measurements when you switch, so a change of network no longer shows up as packet loss and the menu's health reflects the network you are on now. - A host with nothing to ping on the current network (no router, or a DNS server that is the router or one of your other hosts) shows greyed with the reason and does not count towards the overall status. - Settings > Networks lists the networks PingWatch has seen and lets you name them, such as Home or Office. A host can be limited to one network, for devices that only exist there; the menu shows which network you are on. - History can show one network at a time: statistics, charts and the "By hour" view each have a network picker.

- Desktop widget: add PingWatch from Edit Widgets on your desktop. The small widget shows the overall status and the worst host; the medium one shows up to four hosts with their latency, loss and the last few minutes. Click it to open History. macOS decides when widgets redraw, so it can lag the menu bar by a few minutes, and it says so when no update has arrived for 20 minutes or PingWatch is not running. - History has a new "By hour" view for one host over 7 days, 30 days or a custom range of up to 31 days: a row per day and a column per hour, coloured by packet loss or by latency compared with that host's typical hour, so recurring trouble such as busy evenings stands out.

- New installs also watch the DNS server your Mac uses, next to your router, 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8, when it is not one of those. Existing host lists are not changed; you can add it yourself in Settings > Hosts.

- Speed tests now use Apple's own network quality test, built into macOS, and show the speed live while they run: download first, then upload. - Speed tests run only when you click Test now, so they never interrupt a call or a stream. Scheduled tests are gone, including for existing installs. - A test takes up to 30 seconds and fills your connection while it runs. On a fast line it can use a few GB. - History adds a Busy latency column (your latency while the line was full) and shows the full error of a failed test. - Provider (ISP) names are no longer shown. Earlier test results stay in History.

- New hosts ping every 3 seconds by default. Hosts you already have keep their interval. - The packet loss threshold can now be set in steps of 0.1% below 1%, and Settings shows how much one lost ping counts for at each host's interval. - A failed speed test now says why: the HTTP status, which step failed, the Cloudflare location and any wait Cloudflare asked for. Open History to see and copy it. - When Cloudflare refuses speed tests, scheduled tests wait longer before trying again, up to a day, until one succeeds. Test now always runs.
- PingWatch has an app icon: the green health dot from the menu bar.

- On first launch, PingWatch now finds your router from your Mac's network instead of assuming 10.0.0.1. - Scheduled speed tests are off for new installs (each test uses about 125 MB). Turn them on in Settings > Speed Test. Existing installs keep their schedule.

First public release.
- Pings your router, 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 (or any hosts you add) every second over ICMP and keeps every result. - The menu bar shows a health dot and the first host's latency; the menu shows latency, jitter and loss per host. - History window with charts and statistics from the last hour to a year, for one host or all of them. - Speed tests against Cloudflare, with the data each test uses. - Updates itself: PingWatch checks once a day and shows "Update available" in its menu.
